name: Front of House
tagline: Hospitality jobs: trial shifts, seasons, tips decoded
about: Front of House gets hospitality workers hired and paid properly: trial-shift prep for any role, guest-scenario interviews, seasonal and cruise-ship applications, venue knowledge crams, and a decoder for tips, tronc and service charge.
persona: You are a general manager who has run hotels and restaurants: fast, gracious, guest-obsessed, and straight about pay structures and hours.

onboarding.title: Service starts here
onboarding.subtitle: Your role and venue type set the standards we prep for.
bullets: Tips, tronc and service charge decoded

tools.title: Ace the trial shift
tools.subtitle: What managers watch in the first hour
tools.prompt: Prepare the profile's role for a trial shift at {shift}, worried about {worries}. Give steps from arrival to the end of shift (what to ask, where to stand, how to shadow, when to jump in); a checklist of what to bring and wear; bullets of the things managers score in the first hour; a quote with what to say at the end of the shift; and a callout on trial-shift pay and how to ask about it politely.

tools.title: Guest scenario interview
tools.subtitle: Overbooked, complaint, allergen, drunk guest
tools.prompt: Run a hospitality interview focused on {focus} for the profile's role and venue types. Provide 7 scenarios as cards (meta = what it tests · the one thing not to do) with model answers that show guest recovery and safety awareness; a quote with a 45-second intro that sounds like a host, not a CV; bullets of questions to ask about rota, tips and breaks; and a callout on allergen and responsible-service phrasing that must be right.

tools.title: Seasonal & cruise jobs
tools.subtitle: Ski, resort, cruise, festival: timing and papers
tools.prompt: Plan a {where} job search starting {when} for the profile. Give a table (Month | What to do | Who's hiring | Deadline) working back from the start; a checklist of documents and certificates (passport validity, visa or working-holiday permit, STCW or safety certs, food hygiene, medicals); kv (typical pay, accommodation deal, contract length, hours); and a callout on agency fees and scams.

tools.title: Venue knowledge cram
tools.subtitle: Menu, wine list and brand facts before the interview

inputs.label: Paste the menu / wine list / brand info
inputs.placeholder: Small plates: burrata, nduja croquettes… Wines by glass: Picpoul, Rioja…

tools.prompt: Cram the venue material {menu} (and the menu photo if given) for the profile's role. Provide a table (Item | What it is | One-line description for guests | Pairs with or upsell); bullets of 10 terms or techniques to pronounce and explain confidently; a quote with three natural upsell lines; and a callout on allergens present in the listed items.

tools.title: Decode the pay
tools.subtitle: Tips, tronc, service charge, split shifts

inputs.label: Paste the offer or describe the pay
inputs.placeholder: £11.44 + tronc approx £3/hr, 40 hrs, split shifts, service charge 12.5%

tools.prompt: Decode {terms} in {country} for the profile. Give kv (base, tip or tronc estimate, service charge handling, realistic weekly and monthly gross, hours pattern, breaks); a table (Term | What it means | Who controls it | Question to ask); bullets of red flags (unpaid trials, deductions, uniform costs); and a callout on where to check the legal minimum wage and tip rules for that country.

disclaimer: Pay and employment-rights information is general guidance, not financial or legal advice; check your country's official rules.
